abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate direction‐of‐arrival (DoA) estimation in real time is essential for stable terahertz (THz) communications. To overcome the limitations of previous diffractive methods that are restricted to 1D sensing or depend on rotation, and to advance their practical deployment, we propose and experimentally validate an all‐optical dual‐angle diffractive neural network (DA‐DNN) capable of simultaneous 2D angular classification. At the heart of our design is a diffractive aperture placed before the neural network as a physical encoder. It converts the phase‐only angular information carried by the incident wave into a complex optical field enriched with amplitude features, thereby producing robust spatial encoding sensitive to angle. The system is modeled using the Rayleigh–Sommerfeld diffraction integral and optimized through end‐to‐end backpropagation. We fabricate a compact, monolithically integrated DA‐DNN device using 3D printing at high resolution and evaluate it through full‐wave simulations and THz experiments that emulate communication environments. The system accurately recognizes 64 angular combinations over a range, providing a passive and scalable optical solution with low latency for THz communications.
title: All‐Optical Dual‐Angle Diffractive Neural Networks for 2D Direction‐of‐Arrival Estimation

abstract: On-device fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs) is becoming increasingly important for personalized AI assistants and adaptive agents. However, standard backpropagation imposes substantial training-state memory overheads that often exceed the stringent resource budgets of mobile platforms. To address this, Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization leverages forward-only probing instead of backpropagation, drastically reducing memory footprints and offering a compelling alternative for on-device adaptation. Nonetheless, scaling ZO fine-tuning to billion-scale trainable parameter spaces remains challenging, as the cost of recovering reliable update directions scales poorly with dimensionality under mobile constraints. In this paper, we present Prism, a mobile-native infrastructure for practical billion-scale on-device ZO fine-tuning. Prism re-architects the ZO loop around a scalable probing substrate, bringing both per-step training latency and memory overhead closer to the inference footprint. We implement Prism end to end on commodity smartphones and evaluate it across diverse tasks and multiple model scales. Prism achieves accuracy comparable to that of state-of-the-art ZO fine-tuning baselines while reducing per-step latency by 53.4%-76.3% and peak memory by 10.6%-13.8% relative to the best baseline in each setting. These results demonstrate the practical feasibility of billion-scale on-device ZO fine-tuning for LLMs under real mobile constraints. We will release our code to support future research.

abstract: THE EL-RAKHAWI FRONTIER QUANTUM INTELLIGENCE FRAMEWORK (EFQIF) by Dr. M.K.A. El-Rakhawi (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23538543) presents five revolutionary pillars addressing critical quantum AI bottlenecks. Key innovations:1. **Topological Quantum Neural Networks (TQNN)**: Utilize anyonic braiding in topological superconductors for passive error resilience, eliminating massive surface-code overhead.2. **Blind Quantum Federated Learning (BQFL)**: Merges Universal Blind Quantum Computing with federated averaging, employing quantum data compression to minimize qubit overhead while ensuring zero-knowledge computation for sensitive medical/financial data.3. **Quantum Neuromorphic Photonics**: Hybrid integrated photonics (TFLN/silicon nitride) leveraging strong χ(2)/χ(3) non-linear effects to mimic synaptic plasticity at room temperature via Mach-Zehnder interferometer meshes.4. **Quantum Cognition Models**: Hardware-accelerated parameterized quantum circuits evolve belief states in Hilbert space, specifically applied to optimize HMI response latency by predicting non-rational user intent patterns.5. **Macro-System QGANs**: Operate on classically derived Reduced-Order Models (ROM) to avoid barren plateaus, optimizing high-dimensional physical systems like fusion reactor magnetohydrodynamics. IP protection excludes abstract quantum phenomena per Alice/Myriad precedents, safeguarding only concrete hardware implementations (topological nanowire layouts, photonic chips, ROM-based QGAN accelerators, HMI-optimized cognition engines), ensuring robust patent eligibility for this post-classical intelligence architecture.
